title: No unknown-field policy for hand-edited issue files (extra keys silently dropped on rewrite)
description:
SPEC's Issue format section and r[schema-valid-issues] never say what happens to keys that are not part of the schema, so the current behavior is serde's default: unknown fields are accepted silently, then destroyed on the next write.

Measured on pebbles 1.0.0 (build of this repo's HEAD): a hand-written issue file containing valid fields plus 'priority: high' and 'assignee: daniel' loads, lists and shows normally, and pebbles never mentions the extra keys. The first operation that rewrites the file (status update, link, convert) serializes from the parsed struct, so both keys are gone with no warning. Meanwhile a *missing* required field ('status') fails the whole file: 'pebbles list' prints 'Warning: Failed to parse issue ...: missing field status' twice and exits 0 with the issue simply absent, and 'pebbles show <id>' errors. So a typo'd key (statuss, title_) reads as success, hides the real problem, and drops data later.

This is the manual-edit path agents take today (README/ARCHITECTURE bless 'jq' and 'edit JSON manually only if the CLI is failing'; see 0d04a3cc). Ask: pick a policy and write it down - either deny_unknown_fields on Issue and Relationship so a hand edit that invents a key is reported at load, or explicitly document that unknown keys are ignored and preserve them across rewrites (e.g. keep a passthrough map in the struct). Then extend r[schema-valid-issues] text and 74499c46 to cover it, since that issue's scope is currently phrased as parse failures only.

Decision: unknown keys are schema violations - detect at load and WARN on every load so users fix the file; deliberately NO preservation/passthrough machinery and NO migration mechanism (user fixes broken data; owner decided 2026-09-22). Unknown keys are schema violations: pebbles must detect them at load and WARN on every load (same channel as the existing parse-failure warnings), so users fix the file. Deliberately NO preservation/passthrough machinery and NO migration mechanism for now - the user fixes broken data. Note: a mutation that rewrites the file still drops unknown keys (serde behavior); the load warning makes that consequence explicit in advance, and 74499c46's schema-compliance reporting covers it. Update SPEC r[schema-valid-issues] text and 74499c46 accordingly (its scope is no longer parse failures only). Implementation detail: report which file and which keys; keep exit 0 on load (degraded-but-usable).
